gap: How the dominant classes c_L and c_R are chosen when the left or right partition has a class-count tie (or the node is multiclass and no class dominates).
options: lowest class index among tied majority classes
the node-level majority class
the class of the nearest example on that side
random tie-break with seed 42
chosen: lowest class index among tied majority classes (deterministic)
rationale: The paper only says 'dominant classes on the left and right sides'; a deterministic tie-break keeps the zero-hyperparameter claim and matches sklearn's np.argmax convention on class-probability vectors.
quote: where cL and cR are the dominant classes on the left and right sides of θ∗ respectively

gap: What happens numerically when δ_M = 0 (e.g. adjacent opposite-class examples coincide, or the feature is duplicated), since w_L = (θ + δ − x_f)/(2δ) divides by zero.
options: treat δ = 0 as decisive hard routing and skip blending
add an epsilon floor to δ
raise an error
chosen: δ = 0 disables the zone at that node (decisive hard routing)
rationale: Consistent with the paper's statement that δ = 0 recovers standard binary CART behaviour; no epsilon is introduced anywhere in the paper.
quote: Setting δ = 0 recovers standard binary CART behaviour.

gap: The 'feature range' used for the 25% clamp is not defined (full dataset vs node subset; raw vs standardised units).
options: max−min of the feature column among the training examples reaching the node
max−min of the feature column over the whole training fold
max−min over the full dataset
chosen: max−min of the feature column among the node's own training examples (in the standardised space used for fitting)
rationale: Section 3.4 states each method receives the node's feature column c ∈ R^n, and clamps are meant to be node-local like δ itself.
quote: clamped to at most 25% of the feature range to prevent degenerate cases

gap: Whether an instance that enters uncertainty zones at two or more nodes on the same path has its child weights multiplied recursively, or whether only the first zone's blend is applied.
options: full recursion: evaluate both subtrees and combine at every zone, multiplying weights down the path
blend only at the topmost zone and use hard routing below
chosen: full recursion with weight multiplication at every zone
rationale: The paper defines the prediction rule per node and notes multi-zone traversal is negligible at depth ≤ 4, so recursion is the faithful reading and differences are numerically tiny.
quote: At depth ≤4, the probability of a single instance traversing two or more uncertainty zones on the same path is negligible in practice.

gap: The exact 5-fold splitter configuration (shuffle on/off, random_state, class stratification details) is not specified, yet credit-g has only 1,000 examples, so fold composition can move decided accuracy by several points.
options: sklearn StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42)
sklearn StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=False) as in the OpenML CC18 task definitions
OpenML task folds via openml.tasks.get_task(...).get_split
chosen: sklearn StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42) as primary; report the unshuffled variant as a sensitivity check
rationale: The paper fixes seeds at 42 but does not state the splitter; OpenML CC18 tasks ship their own folds, which is the other plausible source.

gap: Whether the reported per-dataset value is the mean of per-fold decided accuracies or the pooled decided accuracy over all out-of-fold predictions.
options: mean of the 5 per-fold decided accuracies
pooled decided accuracy over the union of out-of-fold decided predictions
chosen: mean of the 5 per-fold decided accuracies
rationale: The paper describes the values as 5-fold CV means, and mean-of-folds is the sklearn cross_val_score default; the two differ slightly because the decided sets have different sizes per fold.
quote: Results are 5-fold CV means under probabilistic routing.

gap: How credit-g's categorical/nominal attributes are handled: the paper only says features are standardised, implying all 20 columns are used as numeric features for threshold splits.
options: load credit-g from OpenML and treat every column as numeric (sklearn-style axis-aligned thresholds)
one-hot encode nominal columns
ordinal encode categoricals
chosen: load OpenML credit-g as provided and treat all features as numeric (no encoding beyond the dataset's own coding)
rationale: The paper never mentions categorical handling, standardises all features, and uses plain sklearn CART, which only supports numeric splits; standardising implies numeric columns.
quote: Features are standardised within each fold (StandardScaler fitted on training data only)

gap: Whether sample weights are passed to the tree (class balancing) — relevant since mammography is 2.3% positive and credit-g is 70/30 — and whether δ estimators use those same weights.
options: uniform weights everywhere
class_weight='balanced' in both the ternary tree and the CART baseline
balanced only for the neural/medical datasets
chosen: uniform weights everywhere, identical for the ternary tree and the CART baseline
rationale: The paper reports sklearn CART as the baseline with no mention of class_weight, and the margin estimator (Eq. 10) does not use weights at all.
quote: the sample weights w ∈Rn, the optimal threshold θ∗

gap: What to report if a fold produces zero decided instances (possible on small, heavily flagged configurations such as credit-g with class-overlap), since decided accuracy is then undefined.
options: skip the fold and average the remaining folds
fall back to overall accuracy for that fold
report NaN
chosen: skip folds with an empty decided set and average the remaining folds (record how many were skipped)
rationale: Not discussed in the paper; skipping preserves the meaning of 'accuracy restricted to decided instances'.

gap: Minimum node size / stopping rule for growing the depth-4 trees (minimum samples to split, minimum leaf size, whether pure nodes stop early).
options: sklearn defaults (min_samples_split=2, min_samples_leaf=1)
min_samples_leaf tuned to keep δ_NB meaningful
explicit N ≥ 500 rule applied to node-bootstrap
chosen: sklearn CART defaults for both the ternary tree and the baseline
rationale: The paper only fixes max_depth = 4 and compares against a default sklearn DecisionTreeClassifier, so matching defaults keeps the comparison like-for-like.
